How I Work

I approach automation through the lens of an Industrial Engineer. Before touching any tool, I look at the actual process, where the delays happen, where errors creep in, where people are stuck repeating the same manual steps.

From there, I pick whatever tool genuinely fits the problem. Then I build it end to end, test it with real data, and make sure there's a clear record of what happened and why, so nothing gets lost once it's running.

Headshot placeholder
Background

I have a background in Industrial Engineering, which shaped how I approach problems: looking at processes as systems, identifying bottlenecks, eliminating waste, and finding where things break down under pressure.

That way of thinking naturally led me to automation. Across different operations, I kept seeing the same pattern: people spending time on repetitive, error prone work that a well designed system could handle more reliably.

Now I build those systems end to end, designed around the actual problem, tested before deployment, and focused on improving the process rather than simply adding technology.

Aside from automation, here's what else I bring to the table.
